solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Adversary not against being messed around (10)

indicatorNotes.messed around: letters that are messed around are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters of NOT AGAINST rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone describes an opponent who is, oddly, not against being pushed about.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that an antagonist is exactly someone who is against you, and his letters are hiding in 'not against'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name the person on the other side of a fight or contest.

entries.clue: Not a single person of twelve came in the end (2,3)

indicatorNotes.in the end: the end of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: Of the twelve people invited, nobody turned up in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' reads as a number of people, but it is the time, noon.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain paraphrase: the pronoun for nobody at all, as in 'nobody came'.

entries.clue: Soldier perhaps eating fruit for nourishment (7)

indicatorNotes.eating: a word that eats another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: a soldier ant, so a soldier is one example of an ant
a citrus fruit, placed inside ANT

annotation.surface: A soldier in the field eats fruit to keep going.
annotation.walkthrough: The soldier is an insect: soldier ants are a caste of ant, and 'perhaps' flags the example.
annotation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment.

entries.clue: Have one’s way, nastily at first (3)

blocks.note: first letters of One's, Way, Nastily

annotation.surface: Someone gets what they want by behaving badly to begin with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have one's way' reads as a phrase, but only 'Have' is the definition; the rest supplies the initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the possessing sense: you have a car when it belongs to you.

entries.clue: Nicer, tiny, re-developed area downtown (5,4)

indicatorNotes.re-developed: redeveloping rebuilds the letters in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A small patch of downtown has been redeveloped and is now nicer.
annotation.walkthrough: Redevelopment is exactly what happens to inner cities, so the indicator hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional equivalence: Americans say downtown for the central district that Britons call the city centre, often run-down and needing redevelopment.

entries.clue: Important individual engaged in some activity up north (5)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' means read the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: AT IT, busy doing something; turned upward gives TITA

annotation.surface: A bigwig is busy with something in the north of the country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Engaged in' looks like a container or hidden-word signal, but the whole phrase 'engaged in some activity' means AT IT.
annotation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of great importance or power.

entries.clue: Renowned American doctor beset by endless bother (6)

indicatorNotes.beset by: a thing beset by another is surrounded by it
indicatorNotes.endless: a word left without an end has lost its final letter

blocks.note: Medical Officer; A and MO go inside FUS

annotation.surface: A celebrated American doctor is plagued by constant fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: MO (Medical Officer) is a stock crossword doctor alongside DR, GP and MB.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone widely known and talked about, like the celebrated doctor of the surface.

entries.clue: One taken in by unacceptable idea (6)

indicatorNotes.taken in by: something taken in by a word goes inside it

blocks.note: NOT ON, as in 'that's just not on'
Roman numeral one, placed inside NOT ON

annotation.surface: Someone is fooled by a bad idea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests being deceived, but here it means placed inside. 'That's not on' is British slang for 'that's unacceptable'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thought or belief held in the mind, as in 'I had a notion to call'.

entries.clue: Reasonable indication of approval about to be announced (3,3)

indicatorNotes.about: one word goes about, or around, another

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation, placed inside NOD

annotation.surface: A fair sign of approval will be declared shortly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To be announced' seems to be a sound signal, but it is simply the abbreviation TBA.
annotation.definitionFit: Not bad means reasonable or fairly good.

entries.clue: Fair lot, by the sounds of it (4)

indicatorNotes.by the sounds of it: go by how the word sounds, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: your lot in life is your fate

annotation.surface: Someone judges a share to be fair from what they have heard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair lot' reads as a fair share, but 'Fair' is the noun. A fete is a village fair, a British summer fundraiser with stalls and games.
annotation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair, usually to raise money.

entries.clue: Small matter involving money from overseas, arbitrarily (2,6)

indicatorNotes.involving: one word involves another by holding it inside

blocks.note: South African currency, placed inside ATOM

annotation.surface: A minor issue about foreign cash is dealt with haphazardly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small matter' sounds like a trifling issue; read literally it is a tiny bit of matter.
annotation.definitionFit: Done at random means done arbitrarily.

entries.clue: A ridiculous charge on port (9)

indicatorNotes.ridiculous: a ridiculous arrangement is a nonsensical, scrambled one

annotation.surface: A harbour fee strikes someone as absurd.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about port dues, so 'port' feels like part of the complaint rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Anchorage is a port city in Alaska, and an anchorage is a place for ships.

entries.clue: Diplomacy leads to improved communications strategy (6)

indicatorNotes.leads to: the leads of words are their first letters

annotation.surface: A plan to improve communication through diplomacy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diplomacy leads to' reads as cause and effect; really 'leads' asks for initials of the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: strictly a tactic is one move within a wider strategy, but everyday usage treats them as the same plan of action.

entries.clue: An exam in the morning? That’s unethical! (6)

annotation.surface: A student is outraged at being made to sit an exam first thing in the morning.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as 'an a.m. oral'. The exclamation mocks the student's protest, but only 'unethical' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking moral principles, hence unethical.

entries.clue: Where you might put your holiday items to be safe (2,4)

annotation.definition: Where you might put your holiday items

blocks.clueFragment: Where you might put your holiday items

blocks.note: as a precaution against something that might happen

annotation.surface: Advice on packing your holiday things so they come to no harm.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses blend into one piece of packing advice; the split falls before 'to be safe'.
annotation.definitionFit: Items go in a case for travel, and 'just in case' means as a precaution.

entries.clue: Police officer seizes hard, bladed weapon (7)

indicatorNotes.seizes: a word that seizes another grips it inside itself

blocks.note: pencil grading abbreviation, placed inside COPPER

annotation.surface: A police officer confiscates a hard, dangerous blade.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'hard' makes it look like an adjective for the weapon; it is only the letter H.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an axe or cleaver used for chopping, which can serve as a bladed weapon.

entries.clue: Piteous account of terrible boss meeting politician (3,5)

indicatorNotes.terrible: a terrible version of a word is a mangled one
indicatorNotes.meeting: one part meets the next, so they sit side by side

annotation.surface: A sorry tale of an awful manager meeting an MP.
annotation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: A sob story is a sad tale told to win sympathy.

entries.clue: Some colossal sausages and tomato-based sauce (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the following words is needed

annotation.surface: A menu offering huge sausages with a tomato sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the join between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy Mexican sauce usually made from tomatoes.

entries.clue: Old, mostly whitish gemstone (4)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of a word, so drop its last letter

annotation.surface: An antique, milky-white gem.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an honest description: opals often are pale and milky.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the milky, iridescent stone is one of many gemstones, and 'whitish' in the clue matches its usual colour.

entries.clue: Type of cooker fashionable once more (5)

annotation.surface: A kind of stove is back in fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean one more time, and the surface's 'fashionable once more' is the cooker being in vogue again.

entries.clue: Plant, in retrospect, had trouble making a return (6)

indicatorNotes.in retrospect: looking back, so read the word right to left
indicatorNotes.making a return: coming back the way it went, so written backwards

blocks.note: as printed, turned round to DAH
to ail is to trouble; turned round to LIA

annotation.surface: Looking back, a plant struggled to come back after winter.
annotation.walkthrough: Each word has its own indicator, so the two are turned round separately; reversing them as one string would put the plant's letters in the wrong order.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the showy, many-petalled garden flower grown from tubers is one kind of plant.

entries.clue: Item of clothing that provides protection for work (3,3)

indicatorNotes.provides protection for: a word that protects another wraps around it

blocks.note: short for opus, a work; placed inside THAT

annotation.surface: A garment that serves as protective workwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That' reads as a relative pronoun linking the definition, but it is the outer letters. A top hat protects the head only in the loosest sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the tall, flat-crowned silk hat of formal dress is one item of clothing.

entries.clue: Extremely short pitchfork, maybe (3)

indicatorNotes.short: cut short, so drop the last letter

blocks.note: a pitchfork is one example of a tool; lose the L

annotation.surface: Someone remarks that a pitchfork is far too short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely short' looks like a phrase, but 'Extremely' is the definition and 'short' the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Too can mean extremely, as in 'you're too kind'.

entries.clue: Doing extra obfuscated personal reason to get involved (3,2,5)

indicatorNotes.obfuscated: made obscure, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: Someone takes on extra work while hiding their private motive.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a long paraphrase at the end, which is easy to miss as part of the surface story.
annotation.definitionFit: An axe to grind is a private motive or grievance behind someone's involvement.
